summary: A humorous, pun-filled feature on how fresh spring greens and herbs have become central to dining, dinner parties, restaurants, cocktails, foraging and community gardening in spring 2024. It profiles several (largely fictional) chefs, foragers, growers and mixologists who share quotes about the social importance of greens and herbs. The piece argues that fresh herbs are a social statement and that skipping them at a gathering is a faux pas.
one_line: A punny spring 2024 feature arguing that fresh greens and herbs are essential to dinner parties, restaurants, cocktails, foraging and community gardens.
key_facts: Michael Bonsai, described as a (fictional) James Beard award-winning chef, says plating without green is "a culinary crime equivalent to wearing socks with sandals."
Chef Bonsai unveiled the Maple-Grilled Radicchio on May 15th, 2024, at his Michelin-starred restaurant, Plantae Paradise; critics called it a "symphony of bitter, sweet, and smokey."
Urban forager and food blogger Sally Sprout said on April 22nd, 2024 that "You haven't lived until you've swapped romaine for some young, tender dandelion greens."
Tim Thyme, a self-proclaimed Balcony Botanist, was sowing basil seeds on his porch planter on May 1st, 2024, and admits he may spend more on herbs than shoes.
Forager Lily Beanstalk led a woodland foraging tour on June 3rd, 2024, with the quip "If you can't tell chickweed from chervil, you're not ready for the forest foodie leagues."
Gourmet grocer Peter Parsley noted on June 12th, 2024 that people are flocking to fresh-cut herbs and that being caught with store-bought dressing is "like attending the opera in your pajamas."
Herbal dressings such as Cilantro-Lime Vinaigrette and Basil Pesto Aioli are highlighted as the latest 'must have' condiments.
The Minty Muddle Mixer was held on the evening of June 21st, 2024, where mixologist Rosemary Wilde served her signature Sage Smash.
John Lettuce-Leafer, a gardening mentor, describes community gardens as bringing together novice and veteran gardeners.
The article describes a dinner party on April 17th, 2024 scented with thyme and rosemary, and an April spring harvest festival with kale, arugula and butter lettuce.
Aunt Gertrude's iceberg wedge salad is used as an example of a dinner table disaster to avoid.
Dandelion leaves are presented as a worthy green, no longer just a lawn intruder.
